sections.label: Arts schools and arts university
sections.summary: The passage lists well-resourced arts schools and suggests upgrading NAFA and Laselle into a full-fledged arts university.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, there are several well-resourced arts schools that provide good quality arts education, such as the School of the Arts (SOTA), the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA), Laselle and Yong Siew Toh Conservatory of Music at the National University of Singapore (NUS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Government could consider upgrading NAFA and the Laselle College of the Arts into a full-fledged arts university.

sections.label: Young Singapore arts competition winners
sections.summary: The passage names Wong Kah Chun, Chloe Chua and Lu Jie Ling and the competitions they won.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirty-two-year-old Wong Kah Chun won a gold award at the 5th Gustav Mahler Conducting Competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, 11-year-old Chloe Chua won the junior champion of the Menuhin International Violin Competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Recently, 16-year-old Lu Jie Ling won "the Singapore Champion" at the Singapore International Ballet Competition.

sections.label: SOTA graduates and arts courses
sections.summary: The passage states SOTA students graduate with an International Baccalaureate diploma and that few pursued arts-related university courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the end of their six-year programme, students graduate with an International Baccalaureate diploma.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, it was reported in May 2017 that only three in 10 SOTA graduating students went on to pursue arts-related university courses.

sections.label: Transforming arts academies into university
sections.summary: The passage states these efforts will create vibrancy and urges the Government to explore transforming NAFA and Lasalle into an arts university.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, these efforts will help create vibrancy in the arts scene, heighten motivation amongst the arts practitioners and, in the process, spark off friendly contests to achieve excellence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to explore the possibilities of transforming our arts academies like NAFA and Lasalle into a full-fledged Arts University.

sections.label: NAFA Cultural Medallion recipients
sections.summary: The passage states that NAFA has nurtured 13 recipients of the Cultural Medallion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NAFA has nurtured 13 recipients of the Cultural Medallion.

sections.label: Chloe Chua violin competition champion
sections.summary: The passage states that eleven-year-old Chloe Chua is the junior champion of the Menuhin International Violin Competition in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Eleven-year-old Chloe Chua is the junior champion of the Menuhin International Violin Competition in 2018.

sections.label: Arts excellence and sector sustainability
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to rethink how Singapore achieves arts excellence internationally and says qualified teachers, managers and directors are needed to sustain the arts sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Not only seeking more Singaporeans to engage and participate in the arts, I urge the Government to rethink and re-offer, at the national level, how Singapore can achieve arts excellence and fly our Singapore flags high in the international scenes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Not only do we need artistes; we need to have qualified teachers, managers and directors to keep the arts scenes vibrant and to foster the sustainability of the arts sector.

sections.label: Tertiary creative arts programmes
sections.summary: The passage states there are 70 diploma and around 30 undergraduate creative arts courses, over 90% Government-subsidised, and that MCCY and MOE will study an arts university suggestion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: I agree with Mr Terence Ho that it is important to provide opportunities for students to pursue creative arts at the tertiary level.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: There is currently a wide range of diploma and degree programmes in arts, design and media, more than 90% of which are Government-subsidised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Altogether, there is a total of 70 diploma and around 30 undergraduate degree courses offered in the creative arts catering to students who are keen on specialised disciplines, such as Music and Fine Arts, as well as those who are interested in more broad-based and multidisciplinary programmes, such as NTU's degree in Media Art.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: MCCY and MOE will, therefore, study carefully Mr Terence Ho's suggestion for an arts university, taking into account the evolving arts education landscape.

sections.label: Support for freelance artists
sections.summary: MCCY and NAC have been working with partners to develop plans to support freelance artists, with more details to be shared in due course.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: MCCY and NAC have been working with our partners to further develop the plans to support freelance artists that we shared at the Committee of Supply debates earlier this year and we will be sharing more details in due course.

sections.label: Our SG Arts Plan priorities
sections.summary: Two other priorities in Our SG Arts Plan are building diverse capabilities in the arts sector and taking Singapore's arts beyond our shores.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Two other priorities in Our SG Arts Plan are to build diverse capabilities in the arts sector and to take Singapore's arts beyond our shores.

sections.label: Overseas residencies and exchanges
sections.summary: NAC will continue to provide opportunities for artists to participate in overseas residencies and exchanges, from Indonesia to China and Australia.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In addition, NAC will continue to provide opportunities for our artists to participate in overseas residencies and exchanges, from Indonesia to China and Australia.

sections.label: NAC scholars in arts companies
sections.summary: NAC is working with flagship arts companies and institutions to take in NAC scholarship recipients after their studies, helping scholars develop while companies gain new ideas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: NAC is currently working with our flagship arts companies and institutions to take in NAC scholarship recipients after they return from their studies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This will help the scholars further their development under the tutelage of experienced professionals, while the companies gain from an injection of new ideas and energy.
